nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define agricultural crops
nodes.outcome: Define a crop as a plant of the same kind cultivated on a large scale for food or other products.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Classify Kharif and Rabi
nodes.outcome: Classify crops into Kharif and Rabi categories based on the specific seasons of sowing.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: List agricultural practices
nodes.outcome: List the seven basic agricultural practices in their chronological order of execution.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain crop seasonality
nodes.outcome: Explain why certain crops cannot be grown in winter due to specific climatic requirements.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain soil loosening benefits
nodes.outcome: Explain why loosening soil is necessary for root respiration, water absorption, and earthworm survival.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify soil implements
nodes.outcome: Identify diagrams of a plough, hoe, and tractor-driven cultivator used in soil preparation.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Perform seed flotation test
nodes.outcome: Explain the water flotation method to distinguish healthy seeds from damaged ones.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Compare sowing methods
nodes.outcome: Compare the traditional funnel tool with the modern seed drill regarding spacing, depth, and bird protection.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Differentiate manure and fertilizer
nodes.outcome: Define manure and fertilizers and list three differences between them.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain crop rotation
nodes.outcome: Explain the process of crop rotation and how it naturally replenishes soil nitrogen levels.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define irrigation
nodes.outcome: Define irrigation and explain the necessity of a continuous water supply for crop survival.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Describe modern irrigation
nodes.outcome: Describe the operating mechanisms of modern water-saving sprinkler and drip irrigation systems.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain weed impact
nodes.outcome: Explain why weeds compete with crop plants for light, space, and soil nutrients.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: List weeding methods
nodes.outcome: List methods of weeding including manual removal, tilling, and the application of chemical weedicides.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define harvest processes
nodes.outcome: Define harvesting, threshing, and winnowing in the context of cereal grain preparation.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Describe combine harvester
nodes.outcome: Identify the dual role of a 'Combine' machine in simultaneously performing harvesting and threshing.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: State storage precautions
nodes.outcome: State the preventive measures required before storing grains to protect them from moisture, insects, and microorganisms.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Contrast storage methods
nodes.outcome: Differentiate between domestic storage practices and large-scale storage in silos and granaries.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define animal husbandry
nodes.outcome: Define animal husbandry as the agricultural practice of breeding and raising livestock.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: List animal food products
nodes.outcome: List food products obtained from animals and identify their primary nutritional benefits.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Microorganisms
nodes.outcome: Define microorganisms as tiny organisms that cannot be seen with the unaided eye and require a microscope for observation

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Classify Major Groups of Microbes
nodes.outcome: Classify microorganisms into the four major groups: bacteria, fungi, protozoa, and algae

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Describe Characteristics of Viruses
nodes.outcome: Describe viruses as microscopic entities that reproduce only inside the host organism's cells

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Microbial Habitats
nodes.outcome: Identify diverse habitats of microorganisms ranging from ice-cold climates and hot springs to deserts and marshy lands

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Compare Solitary vs Colonial Living
nodes.outcome: Distinguish between microorganisms that live as solitary single cells (like Amoeba) and those that live in colonies (like fungi and bacteria)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain Curd Formation by Lactobacillus
nodes.outcome: Explain how the bacterium Lactobacillus promotes the conversion of milk into curd by multiplying in milk

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Describe Yeast in Baking
nodes.outcome: Describe how yeast reproduces rapidly and produces carbon dioxide gas during respiration, making dough rise and porous

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain Fermentation Process
nodes.outcome: Define fermentation as the process of conversion of sugar into alcohol by yeast

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Antibiotics
nodes.outcome: Define antibiotics as medicines produced from microorganisms that kill or stop the growth of disease-causing microbes

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: State Precautions for Antibiotic Use
nodes.outcome: State the necessary precautions when taking antibiotics, including completing the prescribed course and avoiding unnecessary use

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain Mechanism of Vaccination
nodes.outcome: Explain how introducing dead or weakened microbes into a healthy body triggers antibody production to provide immunity against specific diseases

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Pathogens and Communicable Diseases
nodes.outcome: Define pathogens and explain how communicable diseases spread from an infected person to a healthy person through air, water, food, or physical contact

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Disease Carriers
nodes.outcome: Identify common insect and animal carriers of disease, specifically the housefly for pathogens and the female Anopheles mosquito for malaria parasites

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Match Human Diseases to Microbes
nodes.outcome: Match common human diseases (tuberculosis, measles, cholera, typhoid, polio, hepatitis A) to their causative microorganisms and modes of transmission

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Common Plant Diseases
nodes.outcome: Identify the causative micro-organism and mode of transmission for Citrus canker (bacteria, air), Rust of wheat (fungi, air/seeds), and Yellow vein mosaic of bhindi (virus, insect)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Anthrax and Foot-and-Mouth Disease
nodes.outcome: Identify Anthrax as a bacterial disease affecting humans and cattle and Foot-and-mouth disease as a viral disease of cattle

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain Food Poisoning Cause
nodes.outcome: Explain that food poisoning is caused by the consumption of food spoiled by microorganisms producing toxic substances

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Chemical Food Preservatives
nodes.outcome: Identify common chemical preservatives like sodium benzoate and sodium metabisulphite used to check microbial growth in jams and squashes

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Describe Salt, Sugar, Oil, and Vinegar Preservation
nodes.outcome: Describe how common salt, sugar, and oil/vinegar preserve food by dehydrating cells or creating an environment uninhabitable for bacteria

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain the Pasteurization Process
nodes.outcome: Explain the pasteurization of milk by heating it to about 70°C for 15 to 30 seconds and then suddenly chilling it to prevent microbial growth

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Rhizobium Symbiosis
nodes.outcome: Identify the symbiotic relationship between Rhizobium bacteria living in root nodules of leguminous plants and their role in fixing atmospheric nitrogen

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: State Lightning Nitrogen Fixation
nodes.outcome: State that the physical action of lightning fixes atmospheric nitrogen into compounds of nitrogen in the soil

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Trace the Nitrogen Cycle Steps
nodes.outcome: Trace the path of nitrogen from atmospheric gas to nitrogenous compounds in soil, absorption by plants, consumption by animals, and breakdown of excreta

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain Role of Denitrification
nodes.outcome: Explain how denitrifying bacteria convert nitrogen compounds in soil back into nitrogen gas, maintaining a constant percentage of nitrogen in the atmosphere

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Natural Resources
nodes.outcome: Define natural resources as materials obtained from nature and used by living organisms.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Man-Made Resources
nodes.outcome: Define man-made resources as human-created materials derived through processing natural substances.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Classify Resources as Natural or Man-Made
nodes.outcome: Classify a given list of daily materials into natural and man-made resources.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Inexhaustible Natural Resources
nodes.outcome: Define inexhaustible natural resources as resources present in unlimited quantity in nature that are not likely to be exhausted by human activities.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Inexhaustible Resources Examples
nodes.outcome: Identify sunlight and air as examples of inexhaustible natural resources.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Exhaustible Natural Resources
nodes.outcome: Define exhaustible natural resources as resources present in limited quantity in nature that can be exhausted by human activities.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Exhaustible Resources Examples
nodes.outcome: Identify forests, wildlife, minerals, coal, petroleum, and natural gas as examples of exhaustible natural resources.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Fossil Fuels
nodes.outcome: Define fossil fuels as exhaustible energy sources formed from the dead remains of living organisms over millions of years.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: List Major Fossil Fuels
nodes.outcome: List coal, petroleum, and natural gas as the three major types of fossil fuels.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Describe Physical Properties of Coal
nodes.outcome: State the physical properties of coal as a hard, black-coloured combustible substance.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: State Traditional Uses of Coal
nodes.outcome: State historical and traditional uses of coal, including cooking food and producing steam to run railway engines.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Coal in Thermal Power Generation
nodes.outcome: Identify the role of coal combustion in thermal power plants to produce electricity.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Precursor Material of Coal
nodes.outcome: Identify dense forests and wetlands existing around 300 million years ago as the starting material of coal.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Describe Burial of Plant Matter
nodes.outcome: Describe how natural processes like flooding buried forest vegetation under layers of soil, compressing them.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Conditions for Coal Formation
nodes.outcome: State that high temperature, high pressure, and the absence of air deep inside the Earth transformed buried vegetation into coal.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Carbonisation
nodes.outcome: Define carbonisation as the slow chemical process of conversion of dead vegetation into coal under high temperature and pressure.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Gas Produced on Burning Coal
nodes.outcome: State that burning coal in air produces mainly carbon dioxide gas along with heat energy.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Products of Coal Processing
nodes.outcome: State that heating coal strongly in the absence of air yields coke, coal tar, and coal gas.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Describe Properties of Coke
nodes.outcome: Describe coke as a tough, porous, and black substance that is an almost pure form of carbon.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: State Uses of Coke
nodes.outcome: State the industrial uses of coke in the manufacture of steel and in the extraction of many metals.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Describe Properties of Coal Tar
nodes.outcome: Describe coal tar as a black, thick liquid with an unpleasant smell containing a mixture of about 200 substances.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: List Products Derived from Coal Tar
nodes.outcome: List synthetic dyes, drugs, perfumes, plastics, paints, explosives, and naphthalene balls as products derived from coal tar fractions.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Bitumen for Surfacing Roads
nodes.outcome: State that bitumen, a petroleum product, has largely replaced coal tar for metalling the surface of roads.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: State Uses of Coal Gas
nodes.outcome: State that coal gas is used as an industrial fuel in processing plants situated near coal processing units.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Recall Historical Use of Coal Gas for Street Lighting
nodes.outcome: Recall that coal gas was used for street lighting in London (1810) and New York (1820) before transitioning to a heating fuel.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Precursor Material of Petroleum
nodes.outcome: Identify microscopic marine organisms that died and settled at the bottom of the sea as the precursor material for petroleum and natural gas.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Describe Sedimentation of Marine Remains
nodes.outcome: Describe how the remains of dead sea organisms became covered with successive layers of sand and clay over millions of years.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain Transformation to Petroleum and Natural Gas
nodes.outcome: Explain how absence of air, high temperature, and high pressure transformed dead marine organisms into petroleum and natural gas.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Describe Properties of Crude Petroleum
nodes.outcome: Describe crude petroleum as a dark, oily liquid with an unpleasant odour.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Deduce Geological Layering of Oil and Gas
nodes.outcome: Explain why the layer containing petroleum oil and natural gas occurs above water in underground rock formations using density differences.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Recall Early Oil Drilling History
nodes.outcome: State that the world's first oil well was drilled in Pennsylvania, USA (1859), and oil in India was first struck at Makum, Assam (1867).

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Oil-Producing Regions in India
nodes.outcome: Identify Assam, Gujarat, Mumbai High, and the river basins of Godavari and Krishna as major oil-producing regions in India.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Petroleum Refining
nodes.outcome: Define petroleum refining as the industrial process of separating the various constituents or fractions of crude petroleum.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain Principle of Fractional Distillation
nodes.outcome: Explain that fractional distillation separates petroleum fractions based on differences in their boiling point ranges.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: State Uses of LPG
nodes.outcome: State that Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) is used as a fuel for home cooking and in industry.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: State Uses of Petrol
nodes.outcome: State that petrol is used as motor fuel, aviation fuel, and as a solvent for dry cleaning.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: State Uses of Kerosene
nodes.outcome: State that kerosene is used as fuel for stoves, lamps, and jet aircraft.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: State Uses of Diesel
nodes.outcome: State that diesel is used as fuel for heavy motor vehicles like trucks, buses, tractors, and electric generators.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: State Uses of Lubricating Oil
nodes.outcome: State that lubricating oil is used for lubrication of machine parts to reduce friction.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: State Uses of Paraffin Wax
nodes.outcome: State that paraffin wax is used in making ointments, candles, and vaseline.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: State Uses of Bitumen
nodes.outcome: State that bitumen is used in manufacturing paints and for road surfacing.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Match Petroleum Fractions with Uses
nodes.outcome: Match each petroleum fraction (LPG, petrol, kerosene, diesel, lubricating oil, paraffin wax, bitumen) with its corresponding primary use.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Petrochemicals
nodes.outcome: Define petrochemicals as useful commercial chemical substances obtained from petroleum and natural gas.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: State Commercial Applications of Petrochemicals
nodes.outcome: Identify detergents, synthetic fibres (polyester, nylon, acrylic), and plastics (polythene) as commercial products synthesized from petrochemicals.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: State Use of Hydrogen from Natural Gas
nodes.outcome: State that hydrogen gas obtained from natural gas is used in the industrial manufacture of nitrogenous fertilizers (urea).

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain Why Petroleum Is Called Black Gold
nodes.outcome: Explain why petroleum is referred to as 'Black Gold' due to its high commercial and industrial value.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: State Primary Component of Natural Gas
nodes.outcome: State that natural gas consists primarily of methane gas.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Compressed Natural Gas (CNG)
nodes.outcome: Define Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) as natural gas stored and compressed under high pressure.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify CNG in Power Generation
nodes.outcome: State that Compressed Natural Gas is utilized as a fuel for electricity generation.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify CNG as Vehicle Transport Fuel
nodes.outcome: State that CNG is used as fuel for transport vehicles such as cars, buses, and auto-rickshaws.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain CNG Environmental Advantages
nodes.outcome: Explain why CNG is called a cleaner fuel by highlighting that it leaves no residue and causes less air pollution than petrol or diesel.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain Pipeline Transport of Natural Gas
nodes.outcome: Explain why natural gas is advantageous for supply networks because it can be transported directly and efficiently through underground pipes.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Piped Gas Networks in India
nodes.outcome: Identify Vadodara (Gujarat) and parts of Delhi as regions having pipeline networks for domestic and factory gas supply.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Natural Gas Reserves in India
nodes.outcome: Identify Tripura, Rajasthan, Maharashtra (offshore), and the Krishna-Godavari delta as major locations of natural gas reserves in India.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Relate Fossil Fuel Formation Time to Scarcity
nodes.outcome: Explain why fossil fuels cannot be replenished quickly by contrasting their millions-of-years formation timeframe with human consumption rates.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain Impossibility of Lab Synthesis of Fossil Fuels
nodes.outcome: Explain why fossil fuels cannot be prepared in a laboratory by pointing out that natural geological conditions (extreme heat, pressure, deep burial, million-year timescales) cannot be practically replicated.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Infer Limited Lifespan of Known Reserves
nodes.outcome: Infer that the known underground reserves of coal and petroleum will last only a few hundred years at current consumption rates.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Relate Fossil Fuel Combustion to Air Pollution
nodes.outcome: Explain how burning fossil fuels releases unburnt carbon particles, carbon monoxide, and oxides of sulphur and nitrogen that cause air pollution and respiratory problems.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Link Fossil Fuel Combustion to Global Warming
nodes.outcome: Explain how excessive emission of carbon dioxide from fossil fuel combustion enhances the greenhouse effect leading to global warming.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Synthesize Rationale for Judicious Fuel Use
nodes.outcome: Synthesize why fossil fuels must be used judiciously: to ensure availability for future generations, minimize air pollution, and reduce global warming risks.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: State PCRA Full Form and Purpose
nodes.outcome: State that PCRA stands for Petroleum Conservation Research Association and identify its objective of advising citizens on saving fuel.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Apply Constant Speed Tip to Save Fuel
nodes.outcome: Explain why driving at a constant and moderate speed saves petrol and diesel as recommended by PCRA.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Apply Engine Switch-Off Tip
nodes.outcome: Identify traffic lights and waiting points as situations where switching off vehicle engines conserves fuel.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Apply Tyre Pressure and Maintenance Guidelines
nodes.outcome: Explain how ensuring correct tyre pressure and regular vehicle maintenance maximize fuel efficiency based on PCRA guidelines.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Definition of combustion
nodes.outcome: Define combustion as a chemical process in which a substance reacts with oxygen to give off heat and light.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Combustible substances
nodes.outcome: Identify combustible substances as materials that can undergo combustion.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Non-combustible substances
nodes.outcome: Classify common materials into combustible and non-combustible categories.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Air requirement for combustion
nodes.outcome: Demonstrate that air/oxygen is essential for combustion using the inverted glass chimney over a candle experiment.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Heat and light in the Sun
nodes.outcome: Explain that the heat and light produced in the Sun are due to nuclear reactions rather than ordinary chemical combustion.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Respiration as combustion
nodes.outcome: Explain why cellular respiration in living organisms is considered a form of slow combustion.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Definition of ignition temperature
nodes.outcome: Define ignition temperature as the lowest temperature at which a substance catches fire.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Condition below ignition temperature
nodes.outcome: Explain why a combustible substance cannot catch fire as long as its temperature is below its ignition temperature.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Paper cup with water experiment
nodes.outcome: Explain why a paper cup containing water does not burn over a candle flame in terms of heat transfer and ignition temperature.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Composition of matchsticks
nodes.outcome: Name the chemicals present in the modern safety match head (antimony trisulphide and potassium chlorate) and rubbing surface (red phosphorus).

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Working mechanism of a matchstick
nodes.outcome: Trace the chemical sequence triggered by friction when a matchstick is struck against the rough surface.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Inflammable substances definition
nodes.outcome: Define inflammable substances as materials having very low ignition temperature that catch fire easily with a flame.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Examples of inflammable substances
nodes.outcome: List examples of inflammable substances including petrol, alcohol, and LPG.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Three requirements for producing fire
nodes.outcome: State the three essential requirements needed to produce and sustain fire: fuel, air (oxygen), and heat (to raise temperature beyond ignition point).

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Principles of fire fighting
nodes.outcome: Explain how eliminating at least one of the three requirements (fuel, air, heat) stops a fire.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Water as a fire extinguisher
nodes.outcome: Explain how water extinguishes fire by cooling the burning material below its ignition temperature and producing water vapour that blankets the fuel.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Water hazard on electrical fires
nodes.outcome: Explain why water must never be used to extinguish fires involving electrical equipment.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Water hazard on oil and petrol fires
nodes.outcome: Explain why water is unsuitable for extinguishing oil or petrol fires based on relative density.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Carbon dioxide as fire extinguisher
nodes.outcome: Explain why carbon dioxide (CO2) is the best extinguisher for electrical fires and inflammable liquids.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Dual action of CO2 extinguisher
nodes.outcome: Describe the dual action of CO2 in forming a heavy blanket cutting off oxygen and cooling the fuel as it expands rapidly.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Dry powder extinguishers
nodes.outcome: State the use of dry powders of sodium bicarbonate (baking soda) or potassium bicarbonate to produce CO2 near a fire.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Rapid combustion
nodes.outcome: Define rapid combustion as a process in which a substance burns quickly, producing heat and light with external ignition.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Examples of rapid combustion
nodes.outcome: Identify examples of rapid combustion, such as burning of LPG in a kitchen stove or a matchstick.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Spontaneous combustion
nodes.outcome: Define spontaneous combustion as a type of combustion in which a material suddenly bursts into flame without the application of an apparent external heat source.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Spontaneous combustion of phosphorus
nodes.outcome: Explain the spontaneous combustion of white phosphorus at room temperature due to its low ignition temperature.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Spontaneous fires in mines and forests
nodes.outcome: Describe real-world hazards of spontaneous combustion in coal mines and dry forests.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Definition of explosion
nodes.outcome: Define explosion as a sudden reaction accompanied by the evolution of heat, light, sound, and a large volume of gas under pressure.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Combustion in fireworks
nodes.outcome: Classify the ignition of firecrackers and applied pressure triggers as explosion.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Compare types of combustion
nodes.outcome: Compare rapid combustion, spontaneous combustion, and explosion across parameters of external heat required, speed, sound, and gas release.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Condition for flame formation
nodes.outcome: State the principle that only those substances which vaporize during burning produce flames.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Substances producing flame
nodes.outcome: Identify substances that form flames on burning, including kerosene oil and molten wax, because they vaporize.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Substances burning without flame
nodes.outcome: Explain why charcoal and coal glow without forming a flame during combustion based on their inability to vaporize.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Comparison of different flames
nodes.outcome: Compare the appearance, colour, and smoke emission of a candle flame, an LPG stove flame, and a kerosene lantern flame.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Innermost zone of candle flame
nodes.outcome: Identify the innermost zone around the wick as the dark/black zone consisting of unburnt wax vapours.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Temperature of innermost zone
nodes.outcome: State that the innermost zone is the least hot zone of the flame.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Middle zone of candle flame
nodes.outcome: Identify the middle luminous zone as the yellow zone of incomplete/partial combustion.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Temperature of middle zone
nodes.outcome: State that the middle zone is moderately hot.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Outer zone of candle flame
nodes.outcome: Identify the outer non-luminous zone as the blue zone of complete combustion.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Temperature of outer zone
nodes.outcome: State that the outermost non-luminous zone is the hottest part of the flame.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Detection of unburnt carbon particles
nodes.outcome: Demonstrate the presence of unburnt carbon particles in the luminous zone by introducing a clean glass plate into it.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Conducting unburnt wax vapours
nodes.outcome: Demonstrate the presence of wax vapours in the dark zone by passing them through a thin glass tube and lighting them at the other end.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Temperature test using copper wire
nodes.outcome: Explain why a copper wire held just outside the non-luminous zone becomes red hot quickly.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Diagram of candle flame zones
nodes.outcome: Draw and label all three zones of a candle flame indicating their relative heat, colour, and combustion completeness.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Goldsmith blowpipe application
nodes.outcome: Explain why goldsmiths blow the outermost zone of a flame with a metallic blowpipe for melting gold and silver.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Definition of fuel
nodes.outcome: Define a fuel as a substance that produces usable heat energy upon combustion for domestic and industrial purposes.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Classification of fuels by state
nodes.outcome: Classify common fuels into solid (wood, coal), liquid (kerosene, petrol), and gaseous (LPG, CNG, biogas) states.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Characteristics of an ideal fuel
nodes.outcome: List the key characteristics of a good or ideal fuel: readily available, cheap, moderate rate of burning, high heat output, and leaving no undesirable residue.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Absence of a perfect ideal fuel
nodes.outcome: Explain why there is probably no fuel that could be considered a perfect ideal fuel for all situations.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Definition of calorific value
nodes.outcome: Define calorific value as the amount of heat energy produced on complete combustion of 1 kg of a fuel.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Unit of calorific value
nodes.outcome: State the standard unit of calorific value as kilojoules per kilogram (kJ/kg).

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Calculate calorific value or total heat
nodes.outcome: Calculate the calorific value of a fuel given the mass combusted and total heat produced.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Comparison of fuel calorific values
nodes.outcome: Order common fuels (cow dung cake, wood, coal, petrol, kerosene, LPG, biogas, hydrogen) in increasing order of calorific value.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Highest calorific value fuel
nodes.outcome: Identify hydrogen gas as having the highest calorific value (150,000 kJ/kg) among common fuels.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Unburnt carbon and respiratory diseases
nodes.outcome: Explain how unburnt carbon particles from carbon fuels like wood, coal, and petroleum act as dangerous pollutants causing asthma and respiratory disorders.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Carbon monoxide hazard
nodes.outcome: Explain why incomplete combustion produces carbon monoxide gas, a deadly poison that can kill people sleeping in a closed room with a coal fire.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: CO2 emissions and global warming
nodes.outcome: Trace the link between the combustion of carbon-based fuels, increased atmospheric CO2 concentration, and global warming.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Consequences of global warming
nodes.outcome: Describe consequences of global warming such as polar glacier melting, sea-level rise, and coastal flooding.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Formation of acid rain
nodes.outcome: Explain how oxides of sulphur and nitrogen produced from burning coal and diesel dissolve in rainwater to form sulphuric acid and nitric acid.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Harmful effects of acid rain
nodes.outcome: Describe the harmful effects of acid rain on crops, soil, aquatic life, and historical buildings/monuments.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Wood replacement with LPG
nodes.outcome: Compare wood and LPG as domestic fuels in terms of smoke production, calorific value, and environmental impact (deforestation).

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: CNG as a cleaner fuel
nodes.outcome: Explain why CNG is adopted as a cleaner transport fuel replacing petrol and diesel to minimize harmful emissions.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Deforestation from fuelwood usage
nodes.outcome: Explain how cutting trees for fuelwood leads to deforestation and disrupts atmospheric balance.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Paper Strips Vocal Cord Model
nodes.outcome: Demonstrate vocal cord action using two stretched rubber or paper strips blown with air through a slit.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Vocal Cord Tension and Quality
nodes.outcome: Explain how the tightness and thickness of vocal cords change the type and quality of human voice.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Vocal Cord Length Differences
nodes.outcome: Compare the lengths of vocal cords in men (~20 mm), women (~15 mm), and children to explain voice differences.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Need for a Material Medium
nodes.outcome: State that sound requires a material medium (solid, liquid, or gas) to propagate.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Sound Propagation in Air
nodes.outcome: Demonstrate that sound travels through air and its intensity decreases as air is sucked out of a glass tumbler containing a ringing cell phone.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Vacuum
nodes.outcome: Define a vacuum as a space entirely devoid of matter or air.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Sound Cannot Travel in Vacuum
nodes.outcome: Conclude that sound cannot travel through a vacuum.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Trace Bell Jar Experiment
nodes.outcome: Trace the step-by-step observations of an electric bell in an inverted jar as air is evacuated using a vacuum pump.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Communication on the Moon
nodes.outcome: Explain why astronauts cannot hear each other directly on the Moon without radio devices due to the lack of an atmosphere.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Sound Propagation in Liquids
nodes.outcome: Demonstrate that sound travels through liquids by listening to a bell ringing inside a bucket of water without the bell touching the walls.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Aquatic Animal Communication
nodes.outcome: Explain how whales and dolphins communicate underwater using sound transmission through water.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Sound Propagation in Solids
nodes.outcome: Demonstrate sound transmission through solids by tapping one end of a meter scale or wooden table held against an ear.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Toy Telephone Activity
nodes.outcome: Construct and explain a toy string telephone demonstrating sound propagation along a taut thread.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Compare Sound Speeds in Media
nodes.outcome: Order the relative speed of sound propagation across solids, liquids, and gases (fastest in solids, slowest in gases).

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Pinna and Ear Canal Function
nodes.outcome: Identify the funnel shape of the outer ear (pinna) and explain how it collects and channels sound down the ear canal.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Structure of the Eardrum
nodes.outcome: Define the eardrum (tympanic membrane) as a thin, stretched membrane at the end of the auditory canal.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Eardrum Model Activity
nodes.outcome: Construct a working model of the eardrum using a plastic can, stretched rubber balloon, and cereal grains to show vibration upon receiving sound.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Transmission from Eardrum to Inner Ear
nodes.outcome: Trace the transmission of mechanical vibrations from the eardrum through the delicate bones of the middle ear to the inner ear.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Signal Transmission to Brain
nodes.outcome: Explain how the inner ear converts vibrations into electrical signals sent to the brain via the auditory nerve.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Label Human Ear Diagram
nodes.outcome: Label the outer ear (pinna, canal), eardrum, middle ear bones, inner ear (cochlea), and auditory nerve on a diagram of the human ear.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Ear Safety Precautions
nodes.outcome: Explain why inserting sharp, pointed, or hard objects into the ear must be avoided to prevent eardrum rupture and hearing impairment.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Oscillatory Motion
nodes.outcome: Define oscillatory motion as the periodic to-and-fro movement of an object about its mean position.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Amplitude
nodes.outcome: Define amplitude as the maximum displacement of a vibrating particle or object from its central mean position.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Time Period
nodes.outcome: Define time period (T) as the time taken by a vibrating body to complete one full oscillation/vibration.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: SI Unit of Time Period
nodes.outcome: State that the SI unit of time period is the second (s).

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Frequency
nodes.outcome: Define frequency as the number of oscillations or vibrations completed per unit of time (second).

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Unit of Frequency (Hertz)
nodes.outcome: State the SI unit of frequency as Hertz (Hz) and interpret 1 Hz as one oscillation per second.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Calculate Frequency
nodes.outcome: Calculate the frequency of an object given total oscillations and time taken using Frequency = Oscillations / Time.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Relation between Frequency and Time Period
nodes.outcome: State and apply the reciprocal relationship between time period and frequency (T = 1/f or f = 1/T).

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Loudness and Amplitude Relationship
nodes.outcome: State that the loudness of sound depends on its amplitude, where larger amplitude produces louder sound.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Loudness Proportional to Square of Amplitude
nodes.outcome: Apply the rule that loudness is proportional to the square of amplitude (doubling amplitude increases loudness by 4 times).

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Decibel Unit of Loudness
nodes.outcome: State that loudness is measured in decibels (dB) and recall typical levels (whisper ~30 dB, normal talk ~60 dB, traffic ~70 dB).

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Thermocol Ball Amplitude Activity
nodes.outcome: Demonstrate the relationship between strike force, amplitude of vibration (displacement of a suspended thermocol ball), and loudness.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Pitch and Frequency Relationship
nodes.outcome: Explain that pitch (shrillness) of sound is determined by the frequency of vibration, with higher frequency yielding higher pitch.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Compare Pitch: Drum vs Whistle
nodes.outcome: Compare sounds from a drum (low frequency, low pitch) and a whistle (high frequency, high pitch).

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Compare Pitch: Bird chirp vs Lion roar
nodes.outcome: Analyze why a bird's chirp is high pitch (high frequency) but low loudness, while a lion's roar is low pitch (low frequency) but very loud.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Pitch Difference in Adult Male and Female Voices
nodes.outcome: Explain why a woman's voice generally has higher frequency and pitch than a man's voice due to vocal cord differences.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Audible Range for Humans
nodes.outcome: State the audible frequency range of normal human hearing as 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz (20 kHz).

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Infrasonic Sound
nodes.outcome: Define infrasonic sound (infrasound) as sound having frequencies lower than 20 Hz, which is inaudible to humans.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Ultrasonic Sound
nodes.outcome: Define ultrasonic sound (ultrasound) as sound having frequencies higher than 20,000 Hz (20 kHz), inaudible to humans.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Animals and Infrasound/Ultrasound
nodes.outcome: Identify animals capable of hearing or producing infrasound (elephants, whales) and ultrasound (dogs, bats, dolphins).

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Galton Dog Whistle Concept
nodes.outcome: Explain why dogs can respond to special high-frequency Galton whistles that are completely inaudible to human ears.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Applications of Ultrasound Equipment
nodes.outcome: List medical and technological applications of ultrasound equipment operating at frequencies above 20 kHz (e.g. imaging, flaw detection).

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Noise
nodes.outcome: Define noise as unpleasant, jarring, and irregular non-periodic sound.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Musical Sound
nodes.outcome: Define musical sound as pleasant sound produced by regular periodic vibrations.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Differentiate Noise and Music
nodes.outcome: Compare and distinguish noise and musical sound based on regularity of vibrations, pleasing sensation, and source.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Music Becoming Noise at High Volume
nodes.outcome: Explain how musical sound can become noise if its loudness becomes excessively high.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Noise Pollution
nodes.outcome: Define noise pollution as the presence of excessive or unwanted sounds in the environment.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Sources of Noise Pollution
nodes.outcome: Identify major outdoor and household sources of noise pollution (traffic, loudspeakers, construction, mixers, crackers).

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Health Hazards of Noise Pollution
nodes.outcome: List physical and psychological health problems caused by chronic noise exposure, including hypertension, insomnia, anxiety, and hearing impairment.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Types of Hearing Impairment
nodes.outcome: Distinguish between temporary hearing loss due to loud sound exposure and total/permanent congenital hearing impairment.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Silencers and Machine Maintenance
nodes.outcome: Describe engineering controls for noise reduction, such as fitting silencing devices in aircraft engines, transport vehicles, and industrial machines.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Acoustic Shielding with Trees
nodes.outcome: Explain how planting trees along roads and around buildings creates a green belt that absorbs sound and curtails noise pollution reaching homes.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Residential Noise Control Rules
nodes.outcome: Suggest community and personal practices to minimize noise pollution, such as locating factories away from residential zones, lowering TV/music volumes, and minimizing horn usage.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Synthesis of Sound and Acoustic Concepts
nodes.outcome: Synthesize the relationships between vibrating source, wave characteristics (amplitude, frequency), propagation medium, hearing mechanism, and environmental noise control.

nodes.title: Bulb Glowing and Heating Effect

nodes.title: Conductivity of Tap Water

nodes.title: Effect of Dissolved Base in Distilled Water
nodes.outcome: Demonstrate that adding a base (such as sodium hydroxide or potassium hydroxide) makes distilled water conducting

nodes.title: Good Conductors vs Poor Conductors
nodes.outcome: Explain why scientists prefer the classification 'good conductor and poor conductor' over 'conductor and insulator'

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Tectonic Plate Motions
nodes.outcome: Describe the continual movements of tectonic plates including brushing past one another and colliding head-on

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Tectonic Cause of Earthquakes
nodes.outcome: Explain how disturbances caused by tectonic plates brushing past or colliding with each other produce tremors on the Earth's surface

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Non-Tectonic Causes of Tremors
nodes.outcome: List non-tectonic causes of earth tremors including volcanic eruptions, meteor hits, and underground nuclear explosions

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Definition of Seismic and Fault Zones
nodes.outcome: Define seismic or fault zones as the weak boundary boundaries between tectonic plates where earthquakes are most likely to occur

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: High Risk Seismic Zones in India
nodes.outcome: Identify highly vulnerable seismic zones in India including Kashmir, Western and Central Himalayas, North-East, Rann of Kutch, and the Indo-Gangetic Plain

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Definition of Earthquake Focus
nodes.outcome: Define the focus (hypocentre) of an earthquake as the originating point deep inside the Earth's crust where seismic rupture begins

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Definition of Epicentre
nodes.outcome: Define the epicentre as the point on the Earth's surface situated vertically directly above the focus

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Definition of Seismic Waves
nodes.outcome: Define seismic waves as the energy shockwaves generated by an earthquake that travel through the body and surface of the Earth

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Seismograph Instrument and Structure
nodes.outcome: Describe the structure and functioning of a seismograph, consisting of a suspended vibrating pendulum/mass with a pen recording traces on a rotating drum

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Richter Scale Definition and Scale Nature
nodes.outcome: Define the Richter scale as a scale measuring earthquake magnitude and explain that it is logarithmic (non-linear) where an increase of 2 units means 1000 times more destructive energy

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Destructive Magnitude on Richter Scale
nodes.outcome: Classify earthquake severity noting that magnitudes greater than 7 on the Richter scale cause severe destruction to life and structures (e.g. Kashmir and Bhuj > 7.5)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Secondary Disasters from Earthquakes
nodes.outcome: Identify secondary disasters triggered by massive earthquakes including floods, landslides, and tsunamis (e.g. 26 Dec 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Earthquake-Resistant Architecture
nodes.outcome: Describe principles of building design in seismic zones such as using mud/timber instead of heavy masonry, light roofs, and consulting certified architects/engineers

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Indoor Earthquake Safety Measures
nodes.outcome: List indoor safety actions during an earthquake: taking cover under a sturdy table, staying away from tall/heavy objects, and protecting the head with pillows in bed

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Outdoor Earthquake Safety Measures
nodes.outcome: List outdoor safety actions during an earthquake: moving to a clear open area away from tall buildings, trees, and overhead power cables, and remaining inside a stopped vehicle

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Synthesis of Natural Electrical and Seismic Phenomena
nodes.outcome: Compare the nature, predictability, destructive mechanisms, and safety preparedness for atmospheric electrical phenomena (lightning) versus geological phenomena (earthquakes)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Light Requirement for Vision
nodes.outcome: State that an object becomes visible only when light emitted or reflected by it enters our eyes

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Luminous Objects Definition
nodes.outcome: Define luminous objects as objects that emit their own light

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Examples of Luminous Objects
nodes.outcome: Identify examples of luminous objects including the Sun, candle flame, and electric lamp

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Non-Luminous Objects Definition
nodes.outcome: Define non-luminous objects (illuminated objects) as objects that do not emit light but reflect light falling on them

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Illumination of the Moon
nodes.outcome: Explain why the Moon is visible despite being a non-luminous object by referencing reflected sunlight

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Classify Luminous vs Non-Luminous
nodes.outcome: Classify a given set of everyday objects into luminous and non-luminous categories

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Incident Ray Definition
nodes.outcome: Define incident ray as the light ray which strikes any surface

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Reflected Ray Definition
nodes.outcome: Define reflected ray as the light ray which bounces back from the reflecting surface

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Point of Incidence
nodes.outcome: Identify the point of incidence as the point on a surface where the incident ray strikes

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Normal to the Surface
nodes.outcome: Define the normal as the imaginary line drawn perpendicular to the reflecting surface at the point of incidence

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Angle of Incidence Definition
nodes.outcome: Define angle of incidence (i) as the angle between the incident ray and the normal

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Angle of Reflection Definition
nodes.outcome: Define angle of reflection (r) as the angle between the reflected ray and the normal

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: First Law of Reflection
nodes.outcome: State the first law of reflection: the angle of incidence is always equal to the angle of reflection (∠i = ∠r)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Second Law of Reflection
nodes.outcome: State the second law of reflection: the incident ray, the normal at the point of incidence, and the reflected ray all lie in the same plane

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Draw Ray Diagram of Reflection
nodes.outcome: Draw and label a complete ray diagram showing incident ray, reflected ray, normal, angle of incidence, and angle of reflection on a plane mirror

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Calculate Angles in Reflection
nodes.outcome: Calculate the angle of reflection or angle of incidence given the angle between the incident ray and the mirror surface or the other angle

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Normal Incidence on Mirror
nodes.outcome: Predict the path of a ray striking a plane mirror normally along the normal (angle of incidence = 0°)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Plane Mirror Image Characteristics
nodes.outcome: List the characteristics of an image formed by a plane mirror (virtual, erect, same size, and at the same distance behind the mirror as the object in front)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Lateral Inversion Definition
nodes.outcome: Define lateral inversion as the phenomenon where the left side of an object appears as the right side in its mirror image and vice versa

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Application of Lateral Inversion
nodes.outcome: Explain why the word 'AMBULANCE' is written laterally inverted on emergency vehicles using lateral inversion concepts

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Regular Reflection Definition
nodes.outcome: Define regular reflection as reflection from a smooth, polished surface where parallel incident rays are reflected as parallel rays

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Diffused Reflection Definition
nodes.outcome: Define diffused or irregular reflection as reflection from a rough or uneven surface where parallel incident rays are scattered in different directions

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Laws of Reflection in Diffused Reflection
nodes.outcome: Explain why diffused reflection is caused by irregularities in the reflecting surface and does not violate the laws of reflection at individual points

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Compare Regular and Diffused Reflection
nodes.outcome: Compare regular and diffused reflection with respect to surface nature, reflected beam parallelism, and image formation capability

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Multiple Reflection Principle
nodes.outcome: State that light reflected from one mirror can act as incident light on a second mirror to undergo successive reflection

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Barber Shop Mirror Arrangement
nodes.outcome: Trace the path of light enabling a person to see the back of their head in a barber's shop using two facing mirrors

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Periscope Construction
nodes.outcome: Describe the construction of a periscope comprising a tube with two plane mirrors fixed parallel to each other at 45° angles at its bends

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Periscope Working Principle
nodes.outcome: Explain the working mechanism of a periscope by tracing how two successive 90° reflections bend light into the observer's eye

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Uses of Periscopes
nodes.outcome: List practical applications of periscopes in submarines, tanks, and bunkers to view objects outside direct line of sight

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Images in Parallel Mirrors
nodes.outcome: Identify that an infinite number of images are formed when two plane mirrors are placed parallel to each other (angle = 0°)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Multiple Images Formula
nodes.outcome: State the formula N = (360°/θ) - 1 for calculating the number of images formed by two plane mirrors inclined at an angle θ

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Calculate Number of Multiple Images
nodes.outcome: Calculate the number of images formed for two mirrors inclined at angles such as 90°, 60°, 45°, and 120°

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Kaleidoscope Construction
nodes.outcome: Describe the construction of a kaleidoscope using three rectangular plane mirror strips inclined at 60° to form a hollow triangular prism

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Patterns in a Kaleidoscope
nodes.outcome: Explain how multiple reflections inside a kaleidoscope produce symmetrical, ever-changing colourful patterns from broken glass pieces

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Applications of Kaleidoscope
nodes.outcome: State the uses of kaleidoscopes by designers, artists, and wallpaper makers to discover new pattern ideas

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Dispersion of Light Definition
nodes.outcome: Define dispersion of light as the phenomenon of splitting white light into its constituent colours

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Constituent Colours of Sunlight
nodes.outcome: List the seven colours of the visible spectrum in order (VIBGYOR: Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Prism Dispersion Experiment
nodes.outcome: Describe the experiment of passing a narrow beam of sunlight through a glass prism to obtain a colourful spectrum on a white screen

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Water-Mirror Dispersion Activity
nodes.outcome: Explain how a plane mirror inclined in a bowl of water disperses sunlight falling on it onto a white wall

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Rainbow as Natural Dispersion
nodes.outcome: Identify a rainbow as a natural phenomenon showing dispersion of sunlight caused by suspended water droplets in the atmosphere

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Structure and Function of Cornea
nodes.outcome: Identify the cornea as the transparent front spherical part of the eye that protects the eye and lets light enter

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Structure and Function of Iris
nodes.outcome: Describe the iris as the dark muscular diaphragm that gives the eye its distinctive colour and controls pupil size

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Pupil Size Regulation
nodes.outcome: Explain how the pupil contracts in bright light and dilates in dim light to regulate the amount of light entering the eye

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Function of the Eye Lens
nodes.outcome: Identify the convex crystalline lens of the eye and explain its role in focusing light onto the retina

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Retina as Light-Sensitive Screen
nodes.outcome: Describe the retina as the light-sensitive inner lining at the back of the eye where real, inverted images are formed

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Function of Rod Cells
nodes.outcome: Explain that rod cells in the retina are sensitive to dim light (twilight vision) and do not perceive colour

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Function of Cone Cells
nodes.outcome: Explain that cone cells in the retina are sensitive to bright light and are responsible for colour vision

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Compare Rods and Cones
nodes.outcome: Compare rods and cones based on light intensity sensitivity and role in colour perception

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Eye Adaptations in Nocturnal Animals
nodes.outcome: Explain why owls can see clearly at night by relating their large cornea, large pupil, and predominantly rod-packed retina

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Function of Optic Nerve
nodes.outcome: State the function of the optic nerve in transmitting nerve impulses from the retina to the brain

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Blind Spot Definition
nodes.outcome: Define blind spot as the region at the junction of the retina and the optic nerve where no photoreceptor cells exist and vision is impossible

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Demonstrate the Blind Spot
nodes.outcome: Describe the cross-and-dot sheet activity used to demonstrate the presence of the blind spot in the human eye

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Label Diagram of Human Eye
nodes.outcome: Draw and label the structural parts of the human eye: cornea, iris, pupil, lens, retina, ciliary muscle, and optic nerve

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Persistence of Vision Definition
nodes.outcome: Define persistence of vision as the retention of a visual impression on the retina for about 1/16th of a second after the light ceases

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Bird-in-Cage Activity
nodes.outcome: Explain the bird-in-a-cage illusion on a spinning cardboard disc using the principle of persistence of vision

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Persistence in Movies and Animation
nodes.outcome: Explain how projecting still pictures at a rate faster than 16 frames per second (e.g., 24 fps) creates the perception of continuous motion

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Least Distance of Distinct Vision
nodes.outcome: State that the most comfortable distance for reading and clear distinct vision for a normal human eye is about 25 cm

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Healthy Eye Care Habits
nodes.outcome: List essential eye care habits: reading at suitable distance, avoiding direct glare or dim light, washing eyes regularly, and never rubbing eyes

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Cataract Cause and Treatment
nodes.outcome: Describe cataract as the clouding of the eye lens occurring in old age and state that it can be treated by surgically replacing the opaque lens

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Vitamin A and Night Blindness
nodes.outcome: Identify Vitamin A deficiency as the cause of night blindness and list dietary sources rich in Vitamin A (carrots, green leafy vegetables, milk, eggs, papaya)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Optical vs Non-Optical Aids
nodes.outcome: Differentiate between optical aids (lenses, telescopic aids) and non-optical aids (tactile, auditory, electronic aids) for visually impaired individuals

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Braille System Overview
nodes.outcome: Describe the Braille system developed by Louis Braille as a tactile writing system using embossed raised dots for visually impaired individuals

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Braille Dot Patterns and Cell Structure
nodes.outcome: Identify that the Braille system uses cells with two vertical rows of three dots each, yielding 63 distinct dot patterns representing characters, numbers, and grammar signs

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Synthesis of Light, Reflection, and Vision
nodes.outcome: Synthesize concepts of reflection, image formation, and eye anatomy to explain how reflected light forms a recognizable image processed by the brain
